messages.author: dde2d259ec83524b
messages.subject: importing a subset of functions from ggplot2
parts:
Hi,

I've build and am in the process of submitting a bioconductor R
package.
I use ggplot2 to plot heatmaps. I was asked to only import the
functions used
with importFrom (...). I'm struggling with this as, if I import all
the functions used,
there still appears to be other variables/objects declared elsewhere
that I'm unsure
how to include. Any help what be appreciated.

Regards,
Ed

The code for the heatmaps:
p <- ggplot(all.m, aes(variable, GeneNames)) +
geom_tile(aes(fill = value),colour = "white") +
scale_fill_gradient(low = "white", high = "steelblue",
limits = c(0,1)) +
opts(title = "Network Uncertainty", axis.ticks = theme_blank(),
axis.text.x = theme_text(angle = 30, hjust = 1)) +
labs(x = "",y="") +
scale_x_discrete(expand = c(0, 0)) +
scale_y_discrete(expand = c(0, 0)) +
facet_grid( Same ~ ProbType, scales = "free")


The import:
importFrom(ggplot2, ggplot.data.frame, aes, facet_grid, geom_tile,
ggplot, labs, opts,
scale_fill_gradient, scale_x_discrete, scale_y_discrete,
theme_blank, theme_text)

messages.author: 936ef8c6d12fc338
messages.subject: RE: importing a subset of functions from ggplot2
parts:
Dear Ed,

You don't need to use importFrom(). In a package (R, not BioConductor) that I am developing, I added ggplot2 to Suggests: in the DESCRIPTION file. Functions that need ggplot2 to work start with the lines below.

if(!require(ggplot2)){
stop("The ggplot2 package is required for the graphics")
}

Best regards,

Thierry

Is there any reason why they tell you that you must use importFrom()?

Best regards,
